findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There were no signed employee health reporting agreements available for all employees that handle ice. The PIC and owner were unaware that this was a requirement. A follow up is scheduled for 12/29/2025 to ensure that an employee health reporting agreement has been signed for all employees that handle ice. Ensure that once these are signed, that they are kept in a safe, accessible place for all future inspections. Once signed by an employee, they are not required to be updated.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The only employee in the establishment is observed to not be a food handler. The PIC and the owner were unaware that it is a requirement for all employees that handle ice to also be a food handler. This was discussed with both individuals. Ensure that by next routine inspection that all employees that handle ice are a food handler (these expire every three years). 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1050 Observed a nearly full bucket of frothy, molded water beneath the triple sink. Emptied and cleaned during the inspection. There is not an apparent leak at the sink.   All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed a number of drain flies present at the soda gun. The cup and gun appear to be routinely cleaned and are not observed with any accumulative molds. The pests were wiped with a cloth. Advised operator to clean around the drainline. Cup is able to be readily removed for cleaning.  Effective measures to minimize the presence of insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1200 The floor beneath the triple sink is observed damaged. There has been a partial repair of the flooring resulting in unsealed seams and an uneven floor. Opeator indicated a complete repair will occur within the next year. Also, floor behind equipment is littered with chipboard containers and single-service utensils. Clean the floor. All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
The soda gun drain line did not have an air gap.  An air gap was made by cutting the line at 45 degree angle above the drain.
750-1080 The potable water system shall be installed to preclude the possibility of backflow.  Devices to protect against backflow and back siphonage shall be installed at all fixtures and equipment where an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water inlet is not provided between the water outlet from the fixture and the fixture’s flood-level rim and wherever else backflow or back siphonage may occur. Install backflow prevention device.
